findings.paper_title: A2 Appendix B - Treasury Prudential Indicators 2025-26
findings.headline: General Fund financing cost ratio declined to 1.04% in 2026-27 forecast from 2.13% in 2024-25
findings.detail: The ratio of financing costs to net revenue stream for the General Fund fell from 2.13% (2024/25 actual) to 1.96% (2025/26 actual) to 1.04% (2026/27 forecast). This reflects declining debt levels and lower interest rates. Housing Revenue Account financing costs remained higher at 38-41% range.
findings.matters: Financing cost ratios measure affordability of debt; declining ratios mean less revenue is consumed by interest payments, improving financial flexibility and funds available for service delivery.
findings.quote: General Fund 2.13 1.06 1.96 1.04

findings.paper_title: A2 Appendix B - Treasury Prudential Indicators 2025-26
findings.headline: Over 53% of fixed-rate debt matures in 20-30 year bucket, increasing to 58% in forecast
findings.detail: The maturity structure of fixed-rate borrowing shows 53.13% maturing in 20-30 years at 31 March 2026, forecast to increase to 58.12% by 31 March 2027. No debt matures beyond 30 years. This concentration creates a significant refinancing requirement starting around 2045-2055.
findings.matters: Debt maturity concentration affects refinancing risk; high concentration in a single maturity band means substantial refinancing requirement at a specific point in the future, requiring medium-term financial planning.
findings.figures: 20-30 year debt: 53.13% at 31 March 2026, forecast 58.12% at 31 March 2027

findings.paper_title: A2 Appendix B - Treasury Prudential Indicators 2025-26
findings.headline: External debt declining from £30.7m to £25.8m across the period
findings.detail: External debt fell from £30,654k (2024/25) to £28,232k (2025/26) to £25,811k (2026/27), a reduction of £4.8m over two years. This debt reduction occurred while the Council executed its capital programme, indicating delevering funded from internal cash resources.
findings.matters: Declining debt improves credit metrics and repayment capacity; signals the council is reducing reliance on external borrowing and strengthening balance sheet position.

findings.paper_title: A2 Appendix B - Treasury Prudential Indicators 2025-26
findings.headline: Council required zero external borrowing to finance capital programmes in 2025-26 and all years forecast
findings.detail: Despite capital expenditure of £9.7m (General Fund) and £3.4m (HRA) in 2025-26, the net financing requirement from external borrowing was zero for both accounts. Capital was funded entirely from grants, capital receipts, earmarked reserves and direct revenue contributions. Zero external borrowing continues in forecasts for 2026-27.
findings.matters: External borrowing requirement reflects reliance on capital markets; zero borrowing demonstrates capital funding from internal resources and affects the council's available borrowing capacity.
findings.figures: Net Financing need (External Borrowing): £0 for all years, both General Fund and HRA.
findings.quote: Net Financing need (External Borrowing) 0 0 0 0 0

findings.paper_title: A2 Appendix B - Treasury Prudential Indicators 2025-26
findings.headline: General Fund capital expenditure approved at £69.6m delivered £9.7m in 2025-26, with balance carried forward to 2026-27
findings.detail: The Council approved £69,580k for general fund capital expenditure in 2025-26 but achieved only £9,746k (14% of plan). Housing Revenue Account showed similar slippage with £7,312k approved but £3,427k delivered. Both programmes are being re-phased, with 2026-27 budgets amended upwards to £61,406k (General Fund) and £9,295k (HRA) to accommodate carry-forwards.
findings.matters: Capital programme delivery is a key performance measure; significant slippage indicates timing risk in capital spending and affects service provision and forward financial planning.
findings.figures: General Fund 2025/26: £69,580k approved, £9,746k actual. HRA 2025/26: £7,312k approved, £3,427k actual.
findings.quote: Total Capital Expenditure 3,809 69,580 9,746 1,570 61,406

findings.headline: £1.000m allocation for unspecified general capacity lacks explanation
findings.detail: The council is allocating £1.000m to support general capacity within the council, to be spent at the Chief Executive's discretion. No explanation is provided for what capacity constraints exist or why this funding is required at this point.
findings.matters: Unexplained capacity allocations may signal staffing, IT, or operational constraints that could affect service delivery and project execution.
findings.figures: £1.000m allocation for general capacity in 2026/27
findings.quote: in respect of the additional £1.000m set aside to support general capacity within the Council, authorises the Chief Executive, in consultation with the Portfolio Holder for Corporate Finance and Governance, to utilise this funding during the year

findings.headline: Financial planning explicitly framed within interim period before April 2028 unitary authority transition
findings.detail: The council's two-year financial plan is structured around the 1 April 2028 vesting date for the new unitary authority, described as a significant change in the financial landscape. Budget decisions explicitly assess deliverability before March 2028, and the council notes that the outturn position forms an important element of planning for this major organisational change.
findings.matters: Major restructuring creates execution risk; service continuity and project delivery could be disrupted during transition, and the council's ability to maintain financial stability while managing reorganisation is uncertain.
findings.figures: Unitary authority vesting date: 1 April 2028; two-year financial plan extends to this date
findings.quote: the Council's financial position is now being considered within an interim period before new / successor Unitary Councils are established from the current expected date of 1 April 2028

findings.headline: New social housing regulation creating unquantified future costs for Housing Revenue Account
findings.detail: The council notes it remains alert to changes required in managing its housing stock due to the new era of social housing regulation. These impacts will need to be reflected in the 30-year HRA Business Plan, but no specifics or cost projections are provided. The HRA general balance has declined from £4.052m to £3.996m.
findings.matters: New regulatory requirements could require significant HRA spending, and reserves of £3.996m provide limited buffer for unexpected compliance costs.
findings.figures: HRA general balance £3.996m (down from £4.052m); HRA favourable variance £1.652m transferred to balances
findings.quote: Council remains alert to any changes that may be required in managing its housing stock, including the on-going impact from the new era of social housing regulation, which will need to be reflected in the 30 Year Business Plan as necessary

findings.headline: £19.778m in revenue carry-forwards (85% of total variance) remain unsettled and subject to post-outturn review
findings.detail: The council's £23.167m total variance comprises £19.778m in requested carry-forwards and £3.389m final favourable variance. Carry-forwards remain subject to separate review to verify projects support corporate priorities and are deliverable before 31 March 2028. Amounts not subsequently agreed will transfer to corporate investment funds. This high proportion of unresolved spend at year-end is unusual and suggests potential delivery challenges.
findings.matters: Unsettled spend of this magnitude indicates either budget planning issues or execution delays, creating uncertainty about whether planned programmes are realistic and will deliver.
findings.figures: £19.778m carry-forwards of £23.167m total variance; £3.389m final favourable variance
findings.quote: requested revenue carryforwards total £19.778m which remain subject to on-going and separate review. Once the review has been completed and agreed under an existing delegation to the Portfolio Holder for Finance and Governance, the money relating to any items not agreed will be transferred to the relevant Corporate Investment Fund

findings.headline: Bank of England inflation forecast revised to potential 4.5% CPI in 2026, against earlier 2% target forecast for 2026-27
findings.detail: Bank of England's current inflation outlook has shifted significantly. Where they previously expected inflation to reach their 2% target by 2026-27, forecasts now suggest CPI could breach 4.5% in 2026. This represents substantial economic uncertainty that affects council service cost projections and tax base assumptions.
findings.matters: Elevated inflation creates material planning risk for multi-year budgets; service costs and demand pressures will be harder to forecast; council's treasury assumptions about future interest rates and economic environment may require revision
findings.figures: CPI forecast potentially 4.5% in 2026, versus earlier forecast of 2% target by 2026-27
findings.quote: Responding to inflation continues to be a challenge for the Bank of England with their current forecast suggesting CPI could breach 4.5% in 2026, which is a stark contrast to their earlier forecast which suggested inflation would reach their target amount of 2% from 2026/27.

findings.headline: Council invested £6m with another local authority that was later added to Exceptional Financial Support list, gap in counterparty risk review
findings.detail: On 20 March 2026, council placed £6m with another Local Authority for April-October 2026. It was discovered after placing that the counterparty had been added to Central Government's Exceptional Financial Support list in February 2026, but this was not detected before the deal was struck. Council is holding to maturity and states no underlying credit risk, but has implemented process controls to catch this in future.
findings.matters: Shows investment approval process does not validate counterparty risk in real time; while EFS designation carries no direct credit risk per policy, it indicates the council's monitoring of stressed counterparties could miss deterioration between deal placement and funding
findings.figures: £6m investment placed with at-risk counterparty, investment period April-October 2026
findings.quote: Although not a breach of treasury management practices, in 2025/26 there was an investment placed with another Local Authority on 20 March 2026 for £6m for the period from April 2026 to October 2026. Upon review, it was realised that the Local Authority had been added to Central Government's Exceptional Financial Support (EFS) list in February 2026, but this had not been picked up at the time of placing the deal.

findings.headline: Commercial property lease expires in approximately 1 year with council forecasting rental income will decrease
findings.detail: Council holds a £2.136m investment property in Clacton (impaired by £0.076m in 2025-26). The original leasehold occupier ceased trading in 2018 and the property is now sublet. The council has explicitly flagged that rental income 'is likely to decrease based on current market expectations when the current lease expires'. Property value has declined 34% from purchase price over 9 years.
findings.matters: Declining rental income will reduce investment returns council depends on; property has already fallen significantly in value and imminent lease expiration creates timing risk for finding replacement tenant or liquidating at unfavorable price
findings.figures: Property value £2.136m, rental income 2025-26 £0.237m (7% return on purchase price), cumulative impairment £0.076m in 2025-26, lease expiring in ~1 year
findings.quote: It is worth highlighting that as part of developing the forecast / budget, it was recognised that the level of annual rent achievable from this investment property is likely to decrease based on current market expectations when the current lease expires.

findings.headline: Single commercial investment carrying negative net income contribution of -1.28% of net revenue stream (2025/26), improving to -0.43% by 2028/29.
findings.detail: The council has one commercial investment and no service investments. The ratio of commercial investments to net revenue is negative at -1.28% (revised 2025/26), -0.94% (2026/27), and -0.43% (forecast 2027/28-2029), indicating the investment is reducing rather than adding to net revenue. The improving ratio suggests either performance improvement or managed rundown. The document does not explain the nature or reason for the negative contribution.
findings.matters: Negative returns on commercial investment signal either operating losses or strategic capital appreciation strategies that peer councils evaluating commercial ventures need to understand.
findings.figures: Commercial investment ratio: -1.28% (2025/26 revised), -0.94% (2026/27), -0.43% (2028/29 forecast)

findings.committee: Resources and Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: A.1 - Appendix A Annex 1 - Prudential Indicators
findings.headline: Approximately 53% to 63% of outstanding fixed rate debt concentrated in 20-30 year maturity band, with under 13% maturing within two years.
findings.detail: Fixed rate debt maturity analysis shows 53.13% in the 20-30 year band at 31/03/2026, rising to 63.47% by 31/03/2029. Debt maturing within 12 months declines from 8.58% to 4.62%, and 12-24 month maturity band remains stable at approximately 3.9-4.2%. This concentration defers refinancing pressure to 20-30 years ahead but creates a known concentration point.
findings.matters: Lenders assess maturity profile as a key refinancing risk metric; this profile demonstrates prudent debt management avoiding excessive near-term refinancing pressure.

findings.committee: Resources and Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: A.1 - Appendix A Annex 1 - Prudential Indicators
findings.headline: General Fund financing costs declining from 2.13% of net revenue to 0.63%, reflecting improving affordability as debt reduces.
findings.detail: The ratio of financing costs to net revenue stream falls consistently from 2.13% (actual 2024/25) through 1.06% (revised 2025/26), 1.04% (2026/27), 0.78% (2027/28) to 0.63% (forecast 2028/29). This steady decline reflects both declining principal levels and refinancing at prevailing market rates, with significantly more revenue budget headroom by 2028/29.
findings.matters: Shows the council's revenue budget is facing decreasing pressure from debt service, which lenders see as improved affordability for the council.
findings.figures: General Fund financing cost ratio: 2.13% (2024/25 actual) declining to 0.63% (2028/29 forecast)

findings.committee: Resources and Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: A.1 - Appendix A Annex 1 - Prudential Indicators
findings.headline: External debt declining from £30,654k to £23,632k over the forecast period, with Capital Financing Requirement declining from £37,167k to £31,605k.
findings.detail: The council's external debt position shows consistent decline: £30,654k (actual 2024/25) declining through £28,232k (revised 2025/26), £25,811k (2026/27), £24,722k (2027/28) to £23,632k (forecast 2028/29). The Capital Financing Requirement follows the same downward trajectory from £37,167k to £31,605k. Internal borrowing increases from £6,513k to £7,973k, showing the council managing down gross debt while temporarily using cash.
findings.matters: Lenders assess debt trajectory as a key credit metric, and peer councils benchmark their own debt management strategies against councils with clear debt reduction plans.
findings.figures: External debt 2024/25 actual £30,654k declining to 2028/29 forecast £23,632k; CFR declining from £37,167k to £31,605k

findings.committee: Resources and Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: A.1 - Appendix A Annex 1 - Prudential Indicators
findings.headline: General Fund and Housing Revenue Account capital programmes require no external borrowing across entire forecast period.
findings.detail: Both General Fund and HRA capital programmes show Net Financing need (External Borrowing) of 0 for all years 2024/25 through 2028/29. Capital investment is entirely financed from grants, receipts, reserves, and revenue contributions, with no requirement to raise new debt despite significant capital activity in 2025/26.
findings.matters: Indicates the council is managing capital investment within available resources without debt increases, which lenders view as disciplined capital financing and reduced borrowing pressure.
findings.figures: Net Financing need (External Borrowing) = 0 for all years, both General Fund and HRA
findings.quote: Net Financing need (External Borrowing) 0 0 0 0 0

findings.committee: Resources and Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: A.1 - Appendix A Annex 1 - Prudential Indicators
findings.headline: Capital expenditure programme of £68,002k in 2025/26 is fully financed from external grants, receipts and reserves, with no borrowing requirement.
findings.detail: The 2025/26 capital programme of £68,002k is entirely financed from government grants (£48,370k), Disabled Facilities Grant (£12,275k), earmarked reserves (£4,827k), direct revenue contributions (£1,456k), capital receipts (£805k), and Section 106/external contributions (£269k). This represents a significant spike from £3,809k in 2024/25, declining to £1,570k in 2026/27 as external funding sources are exhausted.
findings.matters: Lenders need to assess capital investment sustainability and borrowing needs; peer councils need to understand how external funding cycles affect treasury planning.
findings.quote: Total Capital Expenditure 3,809 68,002 1,570 1,070 1,070

findings.committee: Resources and Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: A.1 - Appendix A - Capital and Treasury Strategy 2026-27
findings.headline: Investment cash reserves depleting at 25% per annum, from £106m to £55m forecast by 2028/29
findings.detail: The council is maintaining an under-borrowed position by using internal cash reserves instead of accessing external borrowing, despite elevated interest rates. Investment balances are forecast to decline from £106.4m (2025/26) through £75m, £61m to £55.5m (2028/29)—a 48% reduction over three years.
findings.matters: Rapid reserve depletion reduces financial flexibility and creates a future refinancing cliff when the council must return to external borrowing markets, potentially at worse rates than currently available.
findings.quote: The Council is currently maintaining an under-borrowed position for the General Fund and the HRA. This means that the capital borrowing need (the Capital Financing Requirement), has not been fully funded with external loans, as cash supporting the Council's reserves, balances and cash flow has been used as a temporary measure.

findings.committee: Resources and Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: A.1 - Appendix A - Capital and Treasury Strategy 2026-27
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation shadow authority from April 2027 creates borrowing authority uncertainty
findings.detail: The council explicitly notes that from April 2027, when the LGR shadow authority takes effect, any future borrowing decisions would require authorisation from the new authority. This uncertainty is influencing current treasury decisions.
findings.matters: Governance transition creates uncertainty about who holds borrowing authority and for how long, affecting the council's ability to manage debt refinancing and capital funding over the next 18 months.
findings.figures: Shadow authority takes effect April 2027
findings.quote: Based on the Government's current timescales, Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) would create a shadow authority from April 2027. Any decision to borrow from that date would need the authorisation of the new authority.

findings.committee: Resources and Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: A.1 - Appendix A - Capital and Treasury Strategy 2026-27
findings.headline: Commercial property investment in Clacton down 34% from original cost, falling further in past six months
findings.detail: The council's investment property purchased in 2017/18 for £3.245m has been written down to £2.212m (31 March 2025) then £2.135m (30 September 2025). The asset is illiquid, held for commercial return, and financed from revenue.
findings.matters: A 34% impairment from original cost on a commercial property signals market deterioration in local real estate and raises questions about income returns versus carrying value and future rental yield.
findings.figures: Original cost £3.245m; March 2025 valuation £2.212m; September 2025 valuation £2.135m; total impairment £1.11m
findings.quote: At 31 March 2025 the carrying value of the property was assessed by the Council's external Valuer at £2.212 million and at 30 September 2025 the carrying value was reduced to £2.135 million

findings.committee: Resources and Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: A.1 - Appendix A - Capital and Treasury Strategy 2026-27
findings.headline: Structural annual deficits 2026/27-2028/29 requiring support from Forecast Risk Fund
findings.detail: The council's three-year forecast shows ongoing annual deficits that are being bridged by a Forecast Risk Fund. This indicates the council cannot balance revenue and expenditure without drawing on contingency funding, signalling structural financial pressure beyond the planning period.
findings.matters: Deficits requiring risk fund support indicate persistent revenue challenges and constrain financial flexibility for managing service changes or unexpected costs.
findings.figures: Annual deficits 2026/27 to 2028/29 supported by Forecast Risk Fund
findings.quote: The latest financial forecast for 2026/27 to 2028/29 reflects annual deficits over the remaining period of the plan, which is supported by the Forecast Risk Fund.

findings.paper_title: A.1 - Report Covering - External Audit Completion Report
findings.headline: Valuation of council's specialised assets remains unresolved from prior year
findings.detail: The auditor has flagged the valuation of a limited number of specialised assets held by the council as an ongoing issue that could not be resolved in the 2024/25 audit. The council and auditors are working together to address this in the 2025/26 audit.
findings.matters: Unresolved asset valuations indicate potential weaknesses in financial reporting processes and suggest the council's balance sheet position may not be fully understood or assured
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: the valuation of a limited number of specialised assets held by the Council. This latter point has previously been discussed with the Committee and remains an on-going issue

findings.paper_title: A.1 - Report Covering - External Audit Completion Report
findings.headline: External auditor will disclaim opinion on 2024/25 accounts due to backstop date constraints
findings.detail: The external auditor anticipates issuing a disclaimed opinion for 2024/25, primarily due to government-imposed backstop dates limiting the scope of audit work. While substantial audit work has been completed, the auditor lacks sufficient evidence to conclude whether the financial statements are free from material misstatement.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion means auditors cannot provide assurance on the financial statements, creating uncertainty about the reliability of the council's reported financial position for lending decisions
findings.figures: Backstop date: 27 February 2026
findings.quote: the External Auditor anticipates issuing a disclaimed opinion for 2024/25

findings.headline: Budget balance relies on Forecast Risk Fund as a non-recurring, time-limited funding source that expires with the council's dissolution on 1 April 2028
findings.detail: The council's balanced budget is underpinned by the Forecast Risk Fund, currently forecast to hold £6.347m by 31 March 2028. This fund is being drawn down to balance the budget and is expected to be depleted by the time the unitary takes over. The two-year financial planning window is explicitly tied to the unitary transition date, with no budget forecast provided for 2028/29 onwards for the current council.
findings.matters: A lender assessing the council's medium-term financial sustainability must understand what happens after April 2028. The current budget balance is achieved in part through drawdown of a fund that will not exist after the unitary is established. This raises questions about whether the underlying budget structure can sustain service delivery on a recurring basis without the one-off funding.
findings.figures: Forecast Risk Fund balance at 31 March 2028: £6.347m; planning window to 1 April 2028
findings.quote: Along with associated business plans, they form an holistic approach to a two-year window leading up to 1 April 2028 (Potential vesting day for the new Unitary authority should Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) proceed on the Government's current timetable for Greater Essex).

findings.headline: Council drawing down £3.4m of earmarked reserves in 2026/27 to balance the budget—a significant increase from the £0.539m drawdown in 2025/26
findings.detail: The council is increasing its reliance on reserves to balance the budget in 2026/27. Earmarked reserve use increases from £0.539m in 2025/26 to £3.4m in 2026/27. While the council maintains £4.0m in uncommitted reserves and £1.758m in NDR Resilience Reserve, the trajectory of increasing annual drawdown raises questions about the underlying budget structure.
findings.matters: Reserves are the financial buffer for contingencies and unexpected costs. When councils draw them down annually to balance budgets, it can indicate structural deficits being masked by non-recurring resources. A lender needs to know whether these annual drawdowns are sustainable or whether they signal underlying budget pressure that will require service reductions or income growth.
findings.figures: 2026/27 reserve drawdown: £3.4m (up from £0.539m in 2025/26); uncommitted reserves: £4.0m; NDR Resilience Reserve: £1.758m
findings.quote: This approach is further supported by the Forecast Risk fund that provides for a fully funded budget over the next two years, as well as acknowledging statutory responsibilities to a successor Unitary Council from as early as 1 April 2028.

findings.headline: Government guidance restricts the council from making major financial decisions—including asset sales, long-term contracts, restructures and reserve spending—until the unitary takes over April 2028
findings.detail: The council is operating under government-issued guidance that prevents it from making decisions that would 'fetter the future decisions of new councils.' This significantly constrains the council's ability to use conventional tools to respond to financial stress or emerging cost pressures. Major asset sales, service restructures, new long-term IT contracts, and changes to benefits schemes are all restricted for the next two years.
findings.matters: A lender assessing the council's financial resilience must understand what tools are available to manage emerging problems. A council unable to dispose of assets, unable to restructure services, and unable to renegotiate long-term contracts has limited ability to respond to financial stress. This reduces the council's financial flexibility significantly.
findings.figures: Planning window constrained until 1 April 2028
findings.quote: it is essential that all involved are cognisant that decisions taken now by existing councils could fetter the future decisions of new councils and act accordingly. Examples of those decisions include but are not limited to the sale and purchase of significant assets, transfer of local assets, entering into new contracts for service delivery including IT procurement, major organisational restructures and changes to staff terms and conditions, establishing companies, undertaking job evaluation, permanent appointments to senior positions, changes to unplanned borrowing and the spending of reserves, and major changes to arrangements such as the local council tax support scheme and council tax exemption scheme.

findings.headline: New waste, recycling and street cleaning contract from April 2026 identified as a significant financial challenge and a financial 'crossroads'
findings.detail: The council explicitly identifies the waste contract as a major cost pressure that, combined with the Local Government Reorganisation transition, represents a critical financial juncture for the next two years. The council has set aside £2.184m from reserves to support this commitment through to the end of 2028/29, but the specific annual cost impact of the new contract is not clearly quantified in the main budget narrative.
findings.matters: Waste and recycling services are typically a substantial budget item, and new contracts frequently bring inflationary pressures. A lender needs to understand whether the council's provision (£2.184m over three years) is adequate for the full cost of the new contract and whether further pressures could emerge.
findings.figures: £2.184m set aside through 31 March 2028 for waste, recycling and street cleaning contract
findings.quote: The cost of the new waste contract from April 2026 presented a significant financial challenge and when taken into account with the potential impact of LGR, which has emerged / evolved since the last forecast was considered, it presents an important financial 'cross roads' that sets the financial context over the next two years

findings.headline: Social Housing (Regulation) Act 2023 introduces new regulatory regime requiring compliance work with cost implications unclear
findings.detail: The council acknowledges the 2023 Act has created 'a new era of regulation for the social housing sector' and states 'work on-going to respond to the necessary activities' within this regime, with costs to be 'reflected in the development of the HRA Business Plan as necessary.'
findings.matters: New regulatory requirements typically require systems investment and operational changes; costs are not yet quantified and could add to the budget pressures already flagged.
findings.figures: No specific budget allocation stated for regulatory response costs
findings.quote: The Social Housing (Regulation) Act 2023 saw the introduction of a new era of regulation for the social housing sector, which the Council remains alert to, with work on-going to respond to the necessary activities within this new regulatory regime, which in turn will be reflected in the development of the HRA Business Plan as necessary.

findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation scheduled for April 2028 creates two-year planning uncertainty and liability transfer risk
findings.detail: Tendring will cease to exist as a district council and be absorbed into a new Unitary Authority from 1 April 2028. The council acknowledges this requires planning its 'financial position within an interim period' and states there will be 'new statutory duties' placed on it through a Structural Changes Order expected by late 2026, including controls on disposals, contracts and reserves.
findings.matters: Organizational dissolution within the loan repayment period creates complexity around liability handover, potential for stranded costs, and uncertainty over which entity is responsible for future HRA obligations.
findings.figures: Reorganisation date 1 April 2028; 24-month planning horizon
findings.quote: The Council's financial position needs to be considered within an interim period before new / successor Unitary Councils are established from the current expected date of 1 April 2028...Similarly to the General Fund, a number of obligations will be placed on the Council and it's Statutory Officers as part of the Government's on-going Local Government Reorganisation reforms for Greater Essex.

findings.headline: Council proposes to fund £0.540m HRA operating deficit in 2026/27 from reserves, acknowledged as not sustainable long-term solution
findings.detail: The council faces a £0.540m operating deficit in 2026/27 and proposes to cover it by drawing from HRA balances rather than cutting expenditure. The council explicitly states this 'is not a sustainable long-term solution' but enables meeting priorities in the immediate term. It expects to move to annual surpluses from 2028/29 onwards.
findings.matters: A council unable to balance its HRA operating budget requires reserve depletion to maintain services, reducing financial flexibility and indicating structural imbalance in income versus spending.
findings.figures: £0.540m deficit, general balance forecast £2.234m at end of 2026/27 (down from the current position after this drawdown)
findings.quote: It is proposed to fund this estimated deficit of £0.540m in 2026/27 by calling money from HRA balances as an alternative to potentially reducing expenditure. It is however recognised that this is not a sustainable long-term solution, but it enables the Council to continue to meet its key priorities in the immediate term

findings.paper_title: A.3 Appendix B - Treasury prudential indicators 2024-25
findings.headline: Investment portfolio average credit score 1.04 against prudential limit of 2.00 in 2024-25
findings.detail: The council maintains a high-quality investment portfolio with an average credit score of 1.04 (2024-25), substantially below the permitted limit of 2.00. This reflects concentration in AAA-rated and government-backed investments (DMO, treasury bills, local authority lending). Score improved from 1.13 in 2023-24.
findings.matters: Lenders monitor counterparty credit risk in council cash management; a score of 1.04 demonstrates conservative positioning that minimises credit loss risk in the investment book
findings.figures: Average credit score 1.13 (2023-24), 1.04 (2024-25 actual), 2.00 (limit)
findings.quote: Average credit score for investments 1.13 1.04 2.00

findings.paper_title: A.3 Appendix B - Treasury prudential indicators 2024-25
findings.headline: Fixed rate debt maturity concentrated at 53.13% in 20-30 year bucket by March 2026
findings.detail: The council's fixed rate debt maturity profile shows more than half of outstanding debt (53.13% by 31/03/2026) maturing in the 20-30 year period, with secondary concentrations in 5-10 years (13.86%) and 24 months-5 years (11.59%). Loans maturing beyond 30 years have reduced to zero by 2026.
findings.matters: Maturity profile determines refinancing risk and timing of cash requirements; heavy concentration in a single 10-year band indicates known borrowing profile but high refinancing volume in that period

findings.paper_title: A.3 Appendix B - Treasury prudential indicators 2024-25
findings.headline: Internal borrowing increasing to £7.4m budgeted for 2025-26 from £6.5m actual in 2024-25
findings.detail: The council is increasing reliance on internal resources to finance capital, with internal borrowing rising from £6,513k (2024-25 actual) to £7,404k (2025-26 planned). This reflects deliberate use of cash and reserves rather than external debt, while external borrowing rates remain elevated relative to investment returns.
findings.matters: Growing internal borrowing indicates either tightening liquidity or strategic choice to avoid external debt markets; it affects cash management and signals council assumptions about near-term borrowing costs
findings.figures: Internal borrowing 2024/25 estimate £6,504k, actual £6,513k; 2025/26 budgeted £7,404k
findings.quote: Internal borrowing 5,299 6,504 6,513 7,404

findings.headline: General Fund financing costs ratio 2.13% actual against 1.39% estimate for 2024-25
findings.detail: The actual ratio of financing costs to net revenue stream reached 2.13%, exceeding the estimate of 1.39% by 74 basis points. Housing Revenue Account remained closer to expectation at 43.91% actual versus 43.35% estimated. The variance indicates borrowing costs or revenue assumptions moved during the year.
findings.matters: Finance directors track cost ratios as affordability measures; variance from estimate signals shifts in either interest costs or revenue base that affect budget sustainability
findings.figures: General Fund 2024/25 estimate 1.39%, actual 2.13%; HRA estimate 43.35%, actual 43.91%
findings.quote: General Fund 2.06 1.39 2.13 1.10

findings.paper_title: A.3 Appendix B - Treasury prudential indicators 2024-25
findings.headline: General Fund capital programme spent £3.8m of £58.7m approved budget in 2024-25
findings.detail: The council approved a General Fund capital programme of £58,743k but spent only £3,809k, delivering less than 7% of planned expenditure. The unspent amount was carried forward into 2025-26 amended budget at £55,668k. Housing Revenue Account performed considerably better at 78% delivery (£7,916k of £10,116k approved).
findings.matters: Significant capital underspend signals project delivery constraints, external dependencies, or scoping issues that affect cash flow, borrowing requirements, and year-on-year capital programming

news_drafts.headline: Tendring's main budget was £3.669m underspent against profile at end of July 2026, papers show
news_drafts.lead:
Tendring Council's General Fund Revenue Account was underspent by £3.669m against its profiled budget at the end of July 2026, according to a budget monitoring report (the in-year check of spending against budget) for the Cabinet meeting of 23 October. The General Fund is the account that council tax and business rates pay into, covering services other than council housing and schools.

A profiled budget is the annual budget spread across the months of the year, so the figure compares actual spending with what the council had planned to have spent by the end of July. The report describes the £3.669m as a net underspend, meaning the total after overspends and underspends on individual budgets are set against each other.

The report says the position reflects the timing of spending across budgets and the timing of Government reimbursements for housing benefit. It does not present the figure as a saving, and the papers give no full-year forecast alongside it.
